_readme: roadmap-supply.py's mapping table for lpt-website, authored 2026-10-13.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. The owner asked for a website that is worked on DAILY and AUTONOMOUSLY,
and he was explicit about the failure mode he does not want: 'not just random one-off fixes, but
a general roadmap of where it's heading, a constant reanalysis and shifting its goals over'.
Before this file, the lpt-website ledger held exactly ONE open item (id 3, the checkout
fast-forward) and nothing read the website's roadmap at all - so the loop had no work supply and
a woken shift would have improvised. This is the deliberate bridge between the roadmap document
and the ledger, and it is the ONLY thing that decides what a website shift is handed.
THE ROADMAP IS THE SPINE. Source doc: docs/website/ROADMAP.md. It holds THEMES (T1-T5), not a
backlog of tweaks, and the checkboxes below are slices of those themes. A shift may re-rank,
split, merge or retire anything in that file - that IS the constant reanalysis - but it must
record what moved and what evidence moved it, in the file's own change log. What a shift may NOT
do is work something the roadmap does not contain without adding it there first, with evidence.
THE STANDING ITEM. The last row's checkbox is deliberately NEVER ticked: roadmap-supply files it
again as soon as the previous one is closed, which is what makes the walk happen every day
without a separate scheduler. Ticking it to make the queue look clean breaks the daily cadence.
FIELDS. key = a lowercase prefix of the checkbox line in src (60 chars, whitespace collapsed),
generated from the document rather than typed. status: filed | blocked | not_filed. host = where
the proving command runs. dod = the exact evidence that counts as done; nothing is filed on this
file's authority alone - a shift that finds a box already true says so and closes it with that
evidence, and never invents work to keep the loop alive.

items.key: busy counter (p1) the screen tells me the pickup shelf is em
items.title: The counter's Out for pickup tile counts the open queue, so it reads 0 while 25 items wait on the pickup shelf
items.why: T1 and a P1 the 2026-10-13 persona walk REPRODUCED mechanically: the label promises the opposite of the number, so the counter tells the staff the pickup shelf is empty while 25 items are READY_FOR_PICKUP. The estate already owns the probe (e2e/personas/verify-pickup-contradiction.mjs), so this is a fix plus a re-run, not new tooling. Filed at 4, not 1: it is a measured P1 in the roadmap's ranked queue but nothing is on fire in production today.
items.dod: DONE requires, quoted: (1) the existing contradiction probe run from the repo root on the host against TEST - `node e2e/personas/verify-pickup-contradiction.mjs` - and the result line that counts as done is the default `/work-orders` 'Out for pickup' number EQUAL to the number `/work-orders?status=READY_FOR_PICKUP` reports for the same store (BEFORE: 0 vs 25), with 'Nothing waiting to be collected' gone while any item is READY_FOR_PICKUP. (2) the BEFORE, quoted verbatim from the roadmap box: default `/work-orders` prints 'Out for pickup 0' and 'Nothing waiting to be collected'; `/work-orders?status=READY_FOR_PICKUP` prints 'Out for pickup 25' and fills the panel with 5. (3) a change-log row appended to docs/website/ROADMAP.md naming both numbers, and the box at :165 ticked ONLY then. The parameter that works is READY_FOR_PICKUP, not OUT_FOR_PICKUP - a run using OUT_FOR_PICKUP has measured nothing.

items.key: owner (p1) the order says the job costs nothing, and tells m
items.title: A work order with no price prints 0.00 USD for both What it costs and Owes instead of saying no price is set
items.why: T1 and a money defect the 2026-10-13 persona walk REPRODUCED on a real order (15ABR8): the panel tells the owner the job costs nothing and that nothing is owed. The probe exists (e2e/personas/semantics-probe.mjs) and reads the panel's own data-testids, so this is a fix plus a re-run, not new tooling. Filed at 4: real, but not a production outage.
items.dod: DONE requires, quoted: (1) the semantics probe run from the repo root on the host against TEST - `node e2e/personas/semantics-probe.mjs` - and the result line that counts as done is the 15ABR8 money panel reporting NO `0.00 USD` beside an unset price: 'What it costs' and 'Owes (the order's own figure)' either both read the same non-zero figure from the same field, or both read blank or 'No price set'. Specifically `data-testid="staff-order-money-owed"` must not print `0.00 USD` when the order has no price. (2) the BEFORE, quoted: both `data-testid="staff-order-money-owed"` and `staff-order-money-paid` read `0.00 USD` with nothing on the screen saying the price is unset (docs/website/walkthroughs/2026-10-13/personas/, semantics-probe.mjs). (3) a change-log row appended to docs/website/ROADMAP.md naming both readings, and the box at :166 ticked ONLY then. A run that only changes the copy without re-reading those testids has not proved the panel.

items.key: the daily walk: walk the test site and the production site w
items.title: THE DAILY WALK: walk test and production with the estate's own walkers, look at the screenshots, and re-rank docs/website/ROADMAP.md against what they show
items.why: The owner's ask, 2026-10-13: 'once a day go through the website and find the top few optimizations, analyze them and document them, and then get to work on them.' The estate ALREADY has the walker - e2e/personas/ (4 viewports x 4 personas, journeys J0-J8, a Walk class that times and counts actions and shoots screenshots), which produced 248 findings (39 major) on 2026-09-25. What was missing is a cadence and something that turns its output into work. This item is the cadence. UPDATED 2026-10-13: the DoD above was written at 01:46 and the persona walk landed at 09:37, so it required only the deterministic floor - the item a shift is HANDED and the roadmap it is told to re-rank disagreed about what the work was. docs/website/ROADMAP.md names the persona walk as the fourth step of this same daily item, and the briefs are in git at e2e/personas/briefs/; the DoD now requires both halves.
items.dod: DONE requires all five, quoted: (1) the DETERMINISTIC FLOOR run against the TEST site - `pnpm personas:walk && pnpm personas:walk:report` - with its report path under e2e/personas/reports/ named in the handoff; (2) the PERSONA WALK run as well, because it is the other half of the pair and the two instruments find different things: one subagent per brief in e2e/personas/briefs/, dispatched per e2e/personas/personas-walk.md, collected with `node e2e/personas/collect.mjs --strict`, with the findings and their screenshots under docs/website/walkthroughs/<YYYY-MM-DD>/personas/ named in the handoff - a run that does only (1) has run the floor and not the walk and does NOT satisfy this item, and a run that does only (2) has no deterministic floor to catch a regression; (3) the screenshots committed under docs/website/walkthroughs/<YYYY-MM-DD>/, with the exact directory listed; (4) a NEW row appended to the change log table in docs/website/ROADMAP.md for today saying what moved and what evidence moved it - a row that only says 'no change' is a valid and honest answer, a MISSING row is not; (5) the top of the ranked queue either unchanged-with-reason or re-ranked-with-evidence. PRODUCTION IS READ-ONLY: public pages and read-only staff screens only. No mutation, no message, no payment, no customer contact, ever, from a walk. If the production walk cannot authenticate, say so and walk production's public pages only - do not skip production silently.

items.key: re-measure the counter at 414x896 and 390x844 with the estat
items.title: Re-measure the counter at 414x896 and 390x844 with the estate's own probe, and state the delta against 2026-10-07
items.why: T1. The staff live in /work-orders on a phone. The estate has already measured this surface: an 11,245px document at 414px, and a counter with NO navigation at all (0 visible links outside the page, 2026-10-07). Whether those numbers still hold is unknown, and measure-counter.mjs already prints every number needed - this is a re-run and a comparison, not new tooling.
items.dod: Run `node frontend/src/features/staff-intake/__probe__/measure-counter.mjs` with PROBE_URL pointed at the test deployment and PROBE_SHOTS at docs/website/walkthroughs/<date>/. DONE requires, quoted: (1) the probe's own printed numbers for pageHeightPx, firstScreen[], targetsUnder44, overflowsRight and hitTest at BOTH widths; (2) those numbers written into docs/website/ROADMAP.md under T1 beside a dated screenshot; (3) an explicit delta line against the 2026-10-07 run, naming each number that changed and each that did not. If the probe will not run, the DONE is a named blocker with the probe's own error text - not a summary.

items.key: reconcile the april audit's 66 findings against today's tree
items.title: Reconcile the 2026-04-20 audit's 66 findings against today's tree and report how many still exist
items.why: T3/T4 and probably the cheapest large win available. docs/audits/ui-ux/IMPLEMENTATION_ROADMAP.md lists 66 findings in five themed phases, written 2026-04-20 and never reconciled since - five months of work has landed on top of it. Its own framing is the owner's own complaint: 'grouped by system/component affinity so that each phase produces a coherent PR rather than scattered drive-by fixes'. Nobody currently knows which of the 66 are already fixed.
items.dod: DONE requires a table with ONE ROW PER FINDING out of the 66, each marked fixed / still present / cannot tell, each with the evidence that settles it (a file:line, a test name, or a screenshot path). The counts go into docs/website/ROADMAP.md under T3 with the date. 'Cannot tell' is an allowed and honest answer for a row; a row with no evidence is not. Do NOT fix anything in this item - its whole value is the count.

items.key: first customer-journey walk on a phone: public site -> servi
items.title: First customer-journey walk on a phone: public site -> service page -> drop-off -> the pay text -> the pay page
items.why: T2, and the theme most likely to hold the biggest wins, with ZERO measurements yet. The pay-before-pickup rail now works end to end (notice -> branded pay page -> card, Zelle or phone -> released) but no one has ever walked it as a CUSTOMER, on a phone, from the public site. This is the journey the shop is actually paid through.
items.dod: DONE requires, quoted: (1) screenshots at 390x844 for EVERY step from the public site to the pay page, committed under docs/website/walkthroughs/<date>/customer-journey/ and each named in the handoff; (2) the wall-clock time and the tap count for the journey recorded as numbers; (3) every point where the walker could not tell what to do next written down as a finding with its screenshot. Do NOT pay anything and do not create a real order to walk it - if a step needs a live order that does not exist on test, that gap is itself the finding.

items.key: first walk of the public site's service pages - t5 - every s
items.title: First walk of the public site's service pages: reachable, priced, and with a path to booking
items.why: T5 and never measured. The shop pays for a website that should be bringing repairs in. Its service pages are the front door and nothing has ever walked them to ask whether each one is reachable, shows a price, and gives a way to book.
items.dod: DONE requires one row per service page naming: reachable (yes/no with the HTTP status), price shown (yes/no), booking path (yes/no), each with a screenshot committed under docs/website/walkthroughs/<date>/service-pages/. The list of pages is to be derived from the site's own sitemap or nav, not from memory - say which, and how many pages it yielded. Pages that do not exist are a finding, not a gap in the list.

items.key: whatever the counter re-measurement exposes, as one coherent
items.title: Whatever the counter re-measurement exposes, as ONE coherent slice of T1
items.why: T1 follow-through, and the item that keeps the loop from becoming the thing the owner objected to. This is deliberately not a specific fix: it is the obligation to turn the counter's measured numbers into a coherent slice of one theme rather than a single drive-by tweak.
items.dod: DONE requires, quoted: (1) the measured numbers that justify the slice, named; (2) the class of problem the slice belongs to stated in one sentence, and why the chosen slice represents it rather than being one instance of it; (3) the change landed on TEST with before/after numbers from the SAME probe command; (4) the roadmap change log row. A slice that cannot state its class does not qualify - do the class instead.

items.key: owner-filed (p3) one public shell: every public page carries
items.title: One public shell: prove every one of the eleven public pages renders the shared nav and footer, and finish the before/after evidence
items.why: T5, and the box the owner himself filed (P3) on 2026-10-13: 'our website is not easy to use, and it is not great.' The fix LANDED - PublicSiteNav + PublicSiteFooter now exist and are rendered by the eleven public pages - but the box is still UNCHECKED because its own done-condition is not met: docs/website/walkthroughs/2026-10-13/owner-feedback/ holds before/after pairs for only TWO of the eleven pages (phone-repair, screen-repair), and the first pass got the count wrong (it said nine and missed /privacy and /terms). The estate already carries the mechanical contract for this in frontend/src/components/landing/__tests__/publicSiteShell.test.tsx, which asserts that all eleven pages render the shell, so this row is a run plus the missing evidence, not new tooling. Filed at 4 rather than the box's P3 so it sits with the other lpt-website rows (4-5) and does not preempt platform work.
items.dod: DONE requires, quoted: (1) the shell contract run from the repo on the host: `cd frontend && pnpm exec vitest run src/components/landing/__tests__/publicSiteShell.test.tsx` and its vitest summary; the result line that counts as done is a summary reporting 13 passed (13) and 0 failed - 2 PublicSiteNav assertions plus 11 page assertions, one per name in that file's PUBLIC_PAGES. ANY failure names the page whose shell is wrong; that is the finding, not a reason to skip the page. (2) every one of those eleven pages shown rendering the shell at 390x844: AFTER screenshots committed under docs/website/walkthroughs/<YYYY-MM-DD>/public-shell/, with the exact directory named in the handoff, and the two pre-fix pairs already in docs/website/walkthroughs/2026-10-13/owner-feedback/ cited as the BEFORE for those two pages - do NOT manufacture a 'before' by reverting code. (3) the eleven-name list in that test compared against the site's own router (every public route reachable without auth in frontend/src/App.tsx), and any public route the list omits named as the finding - the first pass missed /privacy and /terms exactly this way. (4) the box in docs/website/ROADMAP.md ticked ONLY if (1) and (2) both pass, with a change-log row naming that evidence; if one page still fails, leave the box unticked and name that page. A run that reports the test file absent or the suite skipped is NOT done: that is a blocker with the error text quoted.

items.key: owner-filed (p3) a filter must mean what its label says, and
items.title: A filter must mean what its label says: settle the four capped staff lists and the unproven receipt.list, or fix them
items.why: T3 and the owner's own P3 words of 2026-10-14, quoted in the box at docs/website/ROADMAP.md:160. The box is the CLASS and stays unticked on purpose: the instance (the counter's `All statuses` control and the search box that inherited its scope) is FIXED and proven, and the 2026-10-14 second session landed and re-proved four control lies. What is left is named IN the box and is exactly two pieces; the third, (a), is already measured and is NOT re-done here - `node e2e/personas/verify-search-reaches-finished-jobs.mjs` on the DEPLOYED TEST build reports 'PASS: search reached a finished job under `All` (2 row(s)) and did not under `Open` (0).' **THE REACH HALF (b): four lists cap how far any filter or SEARCH can reach, so the same lie reappears in a different shape whenever a match sits past the cap** - PaymentsDashboard.tsx:29 `limit: 20` / :30 `offset: 0` with NO disclosure anywhere in the file, RepairIntakeCasesPage.tsx:25 `limit: 50` with none, StaffIssuesPage.tsx:132 `limit: 100, offset: 0`, TransactionHistoryTab.tsx:259 `limit: 100` / :260 `offset: 0` disclosed only at :1209 as a total. **THE UNPROVEN CONTROL (c): `receipt.list` (ReceiptsTab.tsx:422) is neither honest nor a proven lie** - the handler throws before any query is built (`backend/src/trpc/routers/receipt.router.ts:41`), so no `where` exists to read and no `prisma.receipt.*` list call exists in `backend/src/services/receipt.service.ts`. Authored rather than `not_filed` because these are real, runnable remainders: a `not_filed` row would leave the box counted as `uncovered` and refile the authoring item on every run, the loop this source exists to prevent. Filed at 4, like the rest of this file's rows, so it does not preempt platform work.
items.dod: DONE requires, quoted: (1) a row in docs/website/audits/2026-10-14-all-filters-sweep.md for EACH of the four capped lists and for `receipt.list`, each carrying the `file:line` that sets the cap (or the throw) and the request that path produces, read from the CODE PATH and never from a label - the five sites are re-read at the branch head with `git grep -n -E 'take:|limit:|offset:' -- frontend/src/features/payments/components/PaymentsDashboard.tsx frontend/src/features/repair-intake/pages/RepairIntakeCasesPage.tsx frontend/src/features/admin/pages/StaffIssuesPage.tsx frontend/src/components/payments/TransactionHistoryTab.tsx frontend/src/components/payments/ReceiptsTab.tsx`, and the BEFORE it must print is `29: limit: 20` / `30: offset: 0` in PaymentsDashboard.tsx with no disclosure in the file; `25: limit: 50` in RepairIntakeCasesPage.tsx with none; `132: { status: statusFilter, limit: 100, offset: 0 }` in StaffIssuesPage.tsx; `259: limit: 100` / `260: offset: 0` in TransactionHistoryTab.tsx with its disclosure at `1209: Showing {transactions.length} of {transactionsQuery.data.pagination.total} transactions`; and NO `take`/`limit` in ReceiptsTab.tsx because the handler throws before any query is built. (2) the reach probe run from the repo root on the host against TEST - `node e2e/personas/verify-list-reach.mjs` - printing one line per list of the form `<list> rendered=<n> server_total=<T> disclosure=<text|NONE>`; the result line that counts as done is EVERY line reading either a NON-EMPTY disclosure or `rendered == server_total`: any line reading `disclosure=NONE` with `rendered < server_total` is the finding and FAILS the run. The probe is to be WRITTEN as part of this item - it does not exist yet, and a run reporting it absent is a blocker with the node error text quoted, not a pass. (3) `receipt.list` either PROVEN (a `where` or service method quoted from the code path, with the commit that introduces it) or REMOVED, with the commit named - a sweep row that still says 'unproven' does NOT satisfy it. (4) the box at docs/website/ROADMAP.md:160 ticked ONLY when all four lists and `receipt.list` are settled that way, with a change-log row appended to that file naming the evidence. A run that only quotes the labels, or that fixes one list and calls the rest 'similar', has proved nothing about the class this box exists to close.

items.key: (p1) nothing warns when production falls behind test - t6 -
items.title: Nothing warns when production falls behind test, so verified work stays invisible to customers
items.dod: A read-only check reports main behind test by commit count AND by age, runs on a schedule, and files exactly one owner-readable line naming the drift and the one command that closes it. Proven by planting a drift and watching it report, and proven quiet on a day when main is level with test.
items.why: T6, and the highest-consequence item in this file. MEASURED 2026-10-19: origin/main was 511a7ff5b from 2026-10-16 16:08 while origin/test was 8d71192eb - 74 commits and three days of verified work, including the screen-price table, the public computer finder, the 44px chip fix and the kiosk reload fix. The customer-visible cost was measured on the same page in the same minute: test/screen-repair returns ["$154","$173"] with a 'Screen Repair Prices' table, production /screen-repair returns [] with 0 tables, and /find-a-computer answers the 404 page on production. MERGE HYGIENE rule 2 already forbids accumulation; nothing measured it, so it did not hold. Fixed once by hand on 2026-10-19 (PR #485 -> 6920991e4); this item is the guard that stops it recurring.

items.key: (p1) the faq's answers are not in the document - t5 - measur
items.title: The homepage FAQ's 7,935 answer characters are absent from the DOM, so nothing can find or index them
items.dod: Every answer's text is present in the DOM at load, each question carries a real id anchor, the rows are grouped with a table of contents, a filter input narrows them, and every aria-controls resolves. Proven by a load-time DOM read reporting answer characters > 0, a deep link landing on its own question, and a crawler-style fetch showing the answer text in the HTML.
items.why: T5. MEASURED 2026-10-19 on production: 27 collapsed rows holding 991 question characters and 7,935 answer characters that exist nowhere in the DOM while collapsed - 0 readable, 0 search inputs, 0 anchors; 27 of 27 aria-controls name elements that do not exist. The section is 2,977 px collapsed (41.7% of the homepage; 43% at 393px) and 7,300 px if opened, so answering one question costs up to 27 clicks and Ctrl+F and crawlers see questions only.

items.key: (p1) sitemap.xml advertises three urls while twelve public p
items.title: sitemap.xml lists 3 URLs while 12 public pages exist, and unknown paths answer HTTP 200
items.dod: The sitemap is generated from the route table rather than typed, lists every public route with its canonical host, and an unknown path answers a real 404 status while still rendering the not-found page. Proven by fetching the sitemap and counting entries against the router's public list, and by curl -o /dev/null -s -w '%{http_code}' on an unknown path returning 404.
items.why: T5. MEASURED 2026-10-19: the sitemap lists only /, /privacy and /terms and robots.txt points at it, so the nine public service pages plus /contact, /kosher-flip-phones and /kosher-waze have no discovery path for a search engine. Separately GET /definitely-not-a-route-xyz returns HTTP 200 with a 404 page rendered inside it (a soft 404), which spends crawl budget and tells a crawler every URL is real.

items.key: (p2) /kosher-waze is orphaned and holds the site's only real
items.title: /kosher-waze is linked from nowhere and holds the site's only real price list
items.dod: The page has a real entry point from the homepage and from the footer's Services list, the entry point says what the product is rather than repeating the route name, and a check asserts the link exists so a future shell change cannot orphan it again.
items.why: T5. MEASURED 2026-10-19: /kosher-waze renders 3,588 characters and carries the only actual prices anywhere on the public site (299 for the device, 9 a month for data), and it is linked from nothing - not the homepage, not the footer, not the service pages. Reachable only by typing the URL, so the shop's most differentiated product is invisible to a browsing customer.

items.key: (p2) nothing checks that a section carries the content it na
items.title: Nothing checks that a section carries the content it names, so a heading with nothing under it passes every walk
items.dod: The deterministic floor carries a check that, for each section on each public page, compares the section's child/character/text-node counts against a declared minimum or a named list, fails on a heading-with-nothing-under-it, and was proven by reverting the homepage section to its empty form and watching the check go red, then green after.
items.why: T4. MEASURED 2026-10-19: the homepage 'What We Work On' section rendered a heading, a subtitle and nothing else - 365 characters of HTML, 3 elements, 0 links, 0 images - on production AND test, and had done so since at least 3de71d18d (2026-10-08). The daily walk, persona walk, semantics probe and shared-shell contract all passed throughout, because every one asserts rendering, navigation or clipping and none asserts that a named section has the content its name promises. A section can be present, styled, correctly placed and empty. Fixed by hand in PR #492; this item is the class check.

items.key: (p2) the shop's hours disagree across four surfaces, and one
items.title: The shop's hours disagree across four surfaces, and the footer says 'any time' while Saturday is closed
items.dod: One shared hours component renders on the homepage, the footer, /contact and the FAQ; every surface derives its text from the generated schedule rather than a sentence typed per surface; the Saturday-closed and Friday-cutoff facts appear wherever a customer could act on them; and a contract test fails if any of the four surfaces types its own hours sentence. Proven by the four rendered surfaces agreeing line for line and by a drift test.
items.why: T5. MEASURED 2026-10-19: the footer says 'Drop off any time, every day except Shabbos'; /contact states Saturday Closed as a 7-row <dl>; the FAQ says 'Sundays through Friday at any time' plus 'Fridays until 1.5 hours before sunset'; and the homepage and footer show only the walk-in rows and never mention Saturday or the Friday cutoff. A customer reading the footer can drive to a closed shop. The /contact table is the most complete surface and is the one to converge on.

items.key: (p1) the whole app ships as one bundle: no lazy route, a 3.6
items.title: The whole app ships as one bundle: no lazy route, a 3.66 MB entry chunk
items.dod: Every route below the public landing set loads behind React.lazy with a real fallback, the vendor split is explicit in the Vite config, and the change is proven by measuring the entry chunk and a cold first-load transfer for / at 393x852 BEFORE and AFTER, both numbers in the roadmap file.
items.why: FOUNDATION. MEASURED 2026-10-19: 109 route declarations and ZERO React.lazy, zero route-level dynamic import; only two production dynamic imports exist in 2,296 .ts/.tsx files, both components. No manualChunks, no rollupOptions, no size threshold in any of the 11 Vite configs. The repo's own 2026-10-08 comment records a 3.66 MB entry chunk and lpt-deploy-status.py --live reads today's entry asset at 3.85 MB. A customer on a weak phone downloads the staff counter and the pricing hub before the homepage renders.

items.key: (p2) nothing times out, so a hung request never settles and
items.title: Nothing times out, so a hung request never settles and the retry policy never engages
items.dod: The tRPC link carries an AbortSignal timeout chosen from a measurement of the slowest healthy call; a timed-out request produces a VISIBLE error state rather than a spinner or an empty list; and the `as any` at lib/trpc.ts:55 is removed with tsc --noEmit green. Proven by a forced-slow request showing the error state.
items.why: FOUNDATION. MEASURED 2026-10-19: no per-request timeout on any tRPC link. AbortSignal.timeout appears in exactly three places and none is the client link (hooks/useConnectionMonitor.ts:262, features/communications/hooks/useConnectionHealth.ts:86, features/communications/utils/CircuitBreaker.ts:35). The retry policy is good and single-sourced, which is the point: a request that never settles never reaches it. Same file: lib/trpc.ts:55 casts the whole client `as any`, erasing types at every call site.

items.key: (p2) three different answers for "the primary colour", and t
items.title: Three different answers for the primary colour, and two design-system files that are never loaded
items.dod: One file is the single source of colour, type, spacing and radius; design-tokens.css and components.css are deleted or genuinely imported; docs/design-system.md states the values the site actually ships, checked against the compiled CSS; and a check fails when a new raw hex or arbitrary size is added under components/landing or pages. Proven by the check failing on a planted value and the doc matching built output.
items.why: FOUNDATION. MEASURED 2026-10-19: 80 colour tokens in index.css @theme, while design-tokens.css and components.css are imported by nothing; both tailwind.config.js are inert under Tailwind v4; docs/design-system.md documents blue #2563eb while the site ships navy #0F293F. var(--fs-*) used ONCE across 2,173 files, --space-* 5 times, --radius-* 5 times, against 680 arbitrary Tailwind values and 318 raw hex colours in 86 files. dark: appears 7,410 times across 332 files and is entirely inert - the variant keys off a class nothing sets.

items.key: (p1) on a laptop the first thing to click is below the fold,
items.title: On a laptop the first thing to click is below the fold, and the hours are seven screens down
items.dod: The deployed homepage measured at 1280x720 and 393x852 reports: a primary CTA reachable without scrolling at both, the hours reachable inside the first three viewports or linked from the header, and a hero subhead under 25 words with the fee sentence kept but moved beside the CTA. Proven by before/after geometry taken from the deployed page, not jsdom.

items.title: The global search reads only the newest N matches then slices them, so a real work order cannot be found
items.dod: A query for an old-but-exact work order returns it (ranking over the full match set, not a recency window); a query with eight or more customer matches still returns matching work orders (separate budgets, not one sliced array); the advertised total never exceeds what any page can reach; an error renders an error rather than an empty result; orderNumber is not printed. Proven by four queries against the deployed test host with outputs recorded, plus a forced-error showing the error state.
items.why: LOGIC, and the owner reported the class himself twice. The 2026-10-14 fix corrected the SCOPE (All statuses now means all seven); this is a different live defect. MEASURED 2026-10-19 in backend/src/trpc/routers/search.ts: :146 `const take = size + offset` with :186 orderBy createdAt desc, so only the N NEWEST matching work orders are read from the database; :257-263 ranks that already-truncated set and then slices. The header asks size 8 (searchBarModel.ts:25), so a matching but older work order is never read at all. :217-255 merges customers and orders into ONE array then slices to 8, so eight customer matches return ZERO work orders. :268 computes total from untruncated counts, so the UI prints 'View all N results' for rows no page can reach (/search caps at 25). Also: searchBarModel.ts:119-126 parses 'Work Order #'+orderNumber while docs/decisions/work-order-order-number-internal-only.md:41 says it must never be displayed; and three of four search surfaces fake an answer on failure (GlobalSearch gates on hasResults so an error renders nothing and its 'No results found' is unreachable dead code; UnifiedSearch prints 'No results found' on failure; MobileSearch renders blank).
